correctness.rationale: Haar SO(4) is the pushforward of independent uniform unit quaternions. Conditioning twice gives exact 2nd/4th bilinear-sphere moments. SO(4)×SO(4) invariant quartics are spanned by S², tr((AᵀA)²), detA; three exact matrices fix the coefficients. A standalone 16-variable coefficient checker confirms the resulting identity over 892 monomial positions. The oriented singular-value three-square deficit proves the global lower endpoint and both equality families; Cauchy--Schwarz and AM--GM prove the upper endpoint and its complete equality case. Averaging any candidate Euclidean quadratic norm over left/right proper rotations proves Banach--Mazur optimality. No finite sampling is used to justify a universal quantifier.

originality.rationale: Compared the full mathematical statement, not just title: the closest primary method paper (Collins--Śniady 2004) integrates O(d) polynomial matrix entries but does not optimize this SO(4) Haar fourth-moment ratio or classify both lower equality orbits and the Euclidean distortion. The SO(4) double-cover paper (Fujii--Oike--Suzuki 2006) gives the representation, not the norm theorem. Targeted mathematical-record searches for the exact SO(4) matrix-coefficient statement and its signed-singular-value/determinant aliases returned different Fourier/Walsh/character problems. Novelty remains best-knowledge, not an independence claim.
residual_risks: An older or poorly indexed compact-group norm paper may independently contain the same extrema; independently assessed novelty is not claimed.

value.rationale: The natural full 16-dimensional first matrix-coefficient space of SO(4) has a sharply orientation-sensitive norm geometry: a rank-one coefficient and a full-rank orientation-reversing conformal coefficient share the minimum, while the orientation-preserving conformal orbit gives the maximum. Exact sum-of-squares deficits and optimal Euclidean distortion 2^(1/4) quantify the entire space, not an arbitrary selected coefficient matrix. No dimensional expansion or downstream theorem is needed for this natural exact extremal classification.
